chunks: Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Humran, and from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, all together from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The lowest amount with which the hand of the thief is cut is five dinars.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum value of stolen goods required for cutting the hand of a thief in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the nisab (minimum value) for hadd al-sariqah (hand amputation) at five dinars, reflecting the classical Shia juristic consensus on the threshold for this corporal punishment. It highlights the precision of Shia fiqh in defining material thresholds, distinguishing it from other schools that may use different weights or currencies, and underscores the importance of economic context in applying hudud.
